metadata.case_name: YIU KWOK CHING v. KONG SHUI WAH AND ANOTHER

source: his neck was explored and his right brachial plexus found to be disrupted.

injuries.description: fractured first rib fixed with steel wire
source: A fractured first rib was fixed with steel wire.
On the 9th of December 1978 he had a closed fracture of his right tibia plated.
There was a healing 14 cm. scar on the right skin through which the tibial plate had been recently removed.

injuries.description: keloid and cicatrised scarring at neck and shoulders and tibial surgical scar
injuries.body_part: neck; shoulders; right lower leg (tibial scar)
source: There was a 7 by 15 cm. scar at the root of his neck on the right which was cicatrised and keloid. He had further scars: 2 cm. on the left shoulder following BCG vaccination; 2 cm. and 5 cm. over the right shoulder all of which were keloid. There was a healing 14 cm. scar on the right skin through which the tibial plate had been recently removed.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the neck

manifestations.description: rendered unconscious until waking from an anaesthetic at around 1400 hours on the same day

all motor and sensory innervation of the right upper limb is lost below the level of cervical four; no sensation or function in the limb; hand is claw; gross wasting of pectoral girdle muscles; paralysis of all distal muscles of this limb
hyperaesthesia and pain over the cervical four cutaneous distribution
1 cm. of wasting of the right thigh muscles
can run and hop using the right leg; slight residual angulation of right tibia
multiple keloid scars at root of neck and shoulders and a 14 cm scar on right skin where tibial plate removed

treatments_received: admitted to Fanling Hospital and transferred to Queen Elizabeth Hospital
fixation of fractured first rib with steel wire
transfer to Kowloon Hospital and physiotherapeutic rehabilitation of right leg

losses.description: Right upper limb functionally useless; flail limb; paralysis and loss of sensation and function of the right upper limb.
Keloid and cicatrised scars: 7 by 15 cm scar at root of neck on the right, keloid scars on shoulders, and a healing 14 cm tibial scar.
Cannot walk long distances anymore; slight residual angulation of the right tibia.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Can no longer play football nor swim; formerly played football every two to three days and rode his bicycle; now only hobby is watching television.
Prospects of manual work virtually obliterated by his injury; diminution of future earning capacity.
